guides.name: BPC-157
guides.aka: Body Protection Compound-157, PL 14736, PL-10, Bepecin
guides.dopingStatus: Prohibited by WADA at all times (in and out of competition) under S0, non-approved substances. It was added to the list in 2022.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Not approved as a medicine anywhere, so it is not expected to be registered with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration (DDA). Under Nepal's Drugs Act 2035, drugs must be registered before they are imported or sold.

facts.label: What it is
facts.text: A lab-made chain of 15 amino acids, based on part of a protein first found in human stomach juice.

facts.label: What it was studied for
facts.text: Blood-vessel growth, tendon and tendon-to-bone repair, and healing of the gut lining. These results come from rats and cell experiments, not from people.

facts.label: Human evidence
facts.text: Very little. One small ulcerative colitis trial (reported only as a conference abstract) and three tiny pilot studies. No large human trial has shown it works or is safe.

facts.label: FDA
facts.text: Not approved by the FDA or any other regulator. FDA has raised concerns about immune reactions and peptide impurities. A 2026 FDA advisory panel vote on compounding is not an approval.

guides.summary: BPC-157 is a lab-made chain of 15 amino acids. Rat and cell studies suggest it may help blood vessels grow and tendons heal. It has not been proven in people, it is not an approved medicine anywhere, and WADA bans it in sport.

sections.heading: What BPC-157 is
paragraphs: BPC-157 stands for Body Protection Compound-157. It is a chain of 15 amino acids. It is based on part of a protein first described in human stomach juice.
It is made in a lab. It is not a vitamin, a food or a hormone your body is known to release on its own in this form.
Its research names include PL 14736, PL-10 and Bepecin. Most of the research comes from one group in Croatia, led by Predrag Sikiric.

sections.heading: How it is thought to work in the body
paragraphs: The ideas below come from rat and cell experiments, not from people.

Blood vessel growth: in lab and rat studies, BPC-157 increased the activity of VEGFR2. This receptor tells cells lining blood vessels to grow new vessels. More blood flow can help a damaged area heal.
Cell movement: in tendon cells grown in a dish, BPC-157 switched on the FAK-paxillin pathway. This pathway helps cells crawl and spread, which is how repair cells move into an injury.
Nitric oxide: review papers from the main research group describe effects on the nitric oxide system, which controls how wide blood vessels are.
Short life in the blood: like most natural-style peptides, it is broken down quickly. Reports put its half-life at under 30 minutes in animals.

sections.heading: What the research actually shows
paragraphs: A 2025 systematic review of BPC-157 in sports medicine found 36 studies. Thirty-five were preclinical (animals or cells). Only one was a clinical study in people.
Results in rats with cut or torn tendons, muscle injuries and gut damage were often positive. But rat results often fail to carry over to people.

Human data is very limited: one small ulcerative colitis trial reported only as a conference abstract, and a few tiny pilot studies. No large, controlled human trial has shown that it works or that it is safe.
So the honest summary is: an interesting lead, not a proven treatment.

faq.a: No. No regulator, including the US FDA, has approved BPC-157 as a medicine. A 2026 FDA advisory panel vote on compounding is not an approval.
Yes. WADA has prohibited it at all times, in and out of competition, since 2022 under section S0 (non-approved substances).
We don't know. Almost all of the evidence comes from rats and cells. Only one clinical study was found in a 2025 systematic review of 36 studies.
It is not approved as a medicine anywhere, so it is not expected to be registered with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration.

guides.name: TB-500 (thymosin beta-4 fragment)
guides.aka: Ac-LKKTETQ, a 7-amino-acid piece of thymosin beta-4
guides.dopingStatus: Prohibited by WADA at all times under S2 (growth factors). Thymosin beta-4 and its derivatives, such as TB-500, were added in 2018. It is also prohibited in horse racing.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Not approved as a medicine anywhere, so it is not expected to be registered with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration (DDA). Under Nepal's Drugs Act 2035, drugs must be registered before they are imported or sold.

facts.label: What it is
facts.text: A short lab-made piece (7 amino acids, Ac-LKKTETQ) of the natural protein thymosin beta-4. It is not the full protein.

facts.label: What it was studied for
facts.text: Thymosin beta-4 binds actin, a building block inside cells. In animal and lab studies it helped cells move into wounds. Whether TB-500 does this in people is unknown.

facts.label: Human evidence
facts.text: FDA found no human studies of TB-500. The full thymosin beta-4 protein has been tested in people, for example as eye drops, which is a different product.

facts.label: Combined with BPC-157?
facts.text: Some people combine the two, but no human or controlled study has tested the combination. Any "synergy" is unproven.

sources.title: FDA briefing document on TB-500, Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (July 2026)
Goldstein, Hannappel & Kleinman, Thymosin beta4: actin-sequestering protein moonlights to repair injured tissues (Trends Mol Med 2005, PubMed 16099219)
Philp et al., The actin binding site on thymosin beta4 promotes angiogenesis (PubMed 14500546)
USADA: 2018 Prohibited List, thymosin beta-4 and TB-500 added under S2

guides.summary: TB-500 is a 7-amino-acid lab-made piece of thymosin beta-4, a natural protein that helps cells move. Animal and lab studies of the full protein look interesting, but there are no human studies of TB-500 itself, and WADA bans it.

sections.heading: What TB-500 is
paragraphs: Thymosin beta-4 is a natural protein of 43 amino acids. It is found in almost every cell of the body.
TB-500 is not the full protein. It is a short synthetic piece, Ac-LKKTETQ. This is the stretch of thymosin beta-4 that grabs onto actin.
Because it is only a piece, results from studies of the full protein do not automatically apply to TB-500.

sections.heading: How it is thought to work in the body
paragraphs: Actin is a building block inside cells. Cells join actin units into long fibers to change shape and move.
Thymosin beta-4 holds onto single actin units. It keeps a ready supply on hand, so the cell can build fibers fast when it needs to move.
In lab and animal studies, this helped cells travel into wounds. The actin-binding part of the protein also helped new blood vessels form in lab tests.
Faster cell movement and new blood vessels are two key steps in healing. That is why the protein is studied for repair.

sections.heading: What the research actually shows
paragraphs: The FDA found no human studies of TB-500.
The full thymosin beta-4 protein has been tested in people, for example as eye drops. That is a different product from TB-500.
Some people combine TB-500 with BPC-157. No human or controlled study has tested this combination, so any extra benefit is unproven.

faq.q: Is TB-500 the same as thymosin beta-4?
faq.a: No. Thymosin beta-4 is a 43-amino-acid natural protein. TB-500 is a 7-amino-acid synthetic piece of it (Ac-LKKTETQ).
Yes. WADA has prohibited thymosin beta-4 and its derivatives, such as TB-500, at all times since 2018 under section S2. It is also prohibited in horse racing.

faq.q: Has TB-500 been tested in humans?
faq.a: The FDA found no human studies of TB-500. Human trials have used the full thymosin beta-4 protein, which is a different product.

guides.name: Semaglutide
guides.dopingStatus: Not on WADA's 2026 Prohibited List, but WADA monitors it to look for misuse. Athletes should check current rules with their anti-doping body.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Approved in the US (FDA) and the EU (EMA). We could not confirm its registration with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration. It is a prescription medicine: use only under a doctor's care.

facts.label: Class
facts.text: A GLP-1 receptor agonist: a copy of the gut hormone GLP-1 with a fatty-acid side chain that makes it last about a week.

facts.label: How it works
facts.text: Helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high, lowers glucagon, slows stomach emptying, and acts on appetite areas of the brain.

facts.label: Main trial result
facts.text: In the STEP 1 trial, adults without diabetes lost about 14.9% of body weight over 68 weeks on average, compared with 2.4% on placebo, alongside diet and exercise.

facts.label: Side effects
facts.text: Common: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain. Less common but serious: pancreatitis, gallbladder problems, kidney injury from dehydration. Boxed warning: thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents.

sources.title: Wilding et al., Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity (STEP 1, NEJM 2021; 384:989-1002)
FDA prescribing information for Wegovy (semaglutide)
EMA: Wegovy EPAR
Lau J, et al., Discovery of the Once-Weekly Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) Analogue Semaglutide (J Med Chem 2015)
Aronne LJ, et al., Tirzepatide as Compared with Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity (SURMOUNT-5, NEJM 2025)

guides.summary: Semaglutide is an approved prescription medicine that copies the gut hormone GLP-1 but lasts about a week instead of minutes. It raises insulin when blood sugar is high, lowers glucagon, slows the stomach and reduces appetite. In the STEP 1 trial it cut body weight by about 14.9% on average.

sections.heading: What semaglutide is
paragraphs: Semaglutide is a peptide medicine made to act like GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1). GLP-1 is a hormone your gut releases after you eat.
It is sold as Ozempic (weekly injection for type 2 diabetes), Wegovy (weekly injection for weight management) and Rybelsus (daily tablet for type 2 diabetes).

sections.heading: How it works in the body
paragraphs: Natural GLP-1 lasts only about 2 minutes in the blood. An enzyme called DPP-4 cuts it apart, and the kidneys clear it fast.

Semaglutide fixes this in two ways. One amino acid is swapped so DPP-4 can't cut it. A fatty-acid side chain is added so it sticks to albumin, the main protein in blood. This slows its removal, so it lasts about a week. That is why it is taken once a week.
Pancreas: it helps the pancreas release insulin, but only when blood sugar is high. It also lowers glucagon, a hormone that raises blood sugar.
Stomach: it slows how fast food leaves the stomach, so you feel full for longer.
Brain: it acts on appetite areas in the brain. People feel less hungry and eat less. This is the main driver of weight loss.

sections.heading: What the research shows
paragraphs: In STEP 1, adults with obesity but without diabetes took 2.4 mg weekly for 68 weeks, alongside diet and exercise. They lost about 14.9% of body weight on average. The placebo group lost 2.4%.
In the SURMOUNT-5 head-to-head trial, tirzepatide led to more weight loss than semaglutide: 20.2% vs 13.7% at 72 weeks.
Averages hide wide individual differences. Some people lose much more, others much less.

faq.q: How does semaglutide cause weight loss?
faq.a: Mainly by acting on appetite areas in the brain, so people feel less hungry and eat less. Slower stomach emptying also helps people feel full.

faq.q: Why is semaglutide taken only once a week?
faq.a: One amino acid change protects it from the enzyme DPP-4, and a fatty-acid chain makes it bind to albumin in the blood. Together these stretch its life from minutes to about a week.
No. It is not on WADA's 2026 Prohibited List, but WADA monitors it. Athletes should check current rules with their anti-doping body.
Yes. It is approved in the US and EU as a prescription medicine and should be used only under a doctor's care.

guides.name: Tirzepatide
guides.dopingStatus: Not on the WADA Prohibited List, but covered by WADA monitoring together with semaglutide.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: FDA-approved as Mounjaro (type 2 diabetes) and Zepbound (weight management). We could not confirm its registration with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration. It is a prescription medicine.

facts.label: Class
facts.text: Acts on two gut-hormone receptors: GLP-1 and GIP.

facts.label: How it works
facts.text: Raises insulin release when sugar is high, improves insulin sensitivity, lowers glucagon and slows stomach emptying.

facts.label: Main trial results
facts.text: In SURMOUNT-1, the highest dose gave 20.9% average weight loss at 72 weeks vs 3.1% on placebo. In SURMOUNT-5, tirzepatide led to more weight loss than semaglutide (20.2% vs 13.7%).

sources.title: Jastreboff et al., Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity (SURMOUNT-1, NEJM 2022; 387:205-216)
Aronne et al., Tirzepatide as Compared with Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity (SURMOUNT-5, NEJM 2025; 393:26-36)
FDA: approval of Zepbound for chronic weight management (Nov 2023)
Coskun T, et al., LY3298176, a novel dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (Mol Metab 2018)

guides.summary: Tirzepatide is an approved prescription medicine that acts on two gut-hormone receptors, GIP and GLP-1. It improves blood sugar control and reduces appetite. In SURMOUNT-1 the highest dose cut body weight by 20.9% on average at 72 weeks.

sections.heading: What tirzepatide is
paragraphs: Tirzepatide is a peptide medicine of 39 amino acids. It is sold as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and Zepbound for weight management. It is a once-weekly injection.
Its research code was LY3298176. Eli Lilly makes it.

sections.heading: How it works in the body
paragraphs: Your gut releases two main hormones after a meal that tell the pancreas to release insulin: GLP-1 and GIP. These are called incretins.
Tirzepatide is one molecule that switches on both receptors. In lab studies it acts more strongly on the GIP receptor than on the GLP-1 receptor.
The GLP-1 side works like semaglutide: more insulin when sugar is high, less glucagon, slower stomach emptying and less appetite.
The GIP side adds to the insulin effect and improves insulin sensitivity. Researchers are still working out exactly how GIP adds to weight loss.
A fatty-acid side chain binds it to albumin in the blood. This gives it a half-life of about 5 days, so it can be taken weekly.

sections.heading: What the research shows
paragraphs: In SURMOUNT-1, adults with obesity lost 15.0%, 19.5% and 20.9% of body weight on the 5, 10 and 15 mg doses over 72 weeks. The placebo group lost 3.1%.

In SURMOUNT-5, which compared it directly with semaglutide in 751 adults with obesity, tirzepatide gave 20.2% weight loss vs 13.7% for semaglutide. The trial was open-label and funded by tirzepatide's maker.

faq.q: How is tirzepatide different from semaglutide?
faq.a: Semaglutide acts on one receptor, GLP-1. Tirzepatide acts on two, GLP-1 and GIP. In the SURMOUNT-5 trial, tirzepatide led to more average weight loss (20.2% vs 13.7%).
Yes. The FDA approved it as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and as Zepbound for chronic weight management (November 2023). It is a prescription medicine.
No. It is not on the WADA Prohibited List, but it is covered by WADA monitoring.

guides.name: Retatrutide
guides.dopingStatus: Prohibited in sport at all times. Unapproved drugs like retatrutide fall under WADA's S0 non-approved substances rule, in and out of competition.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Not approved as a medicine anywhere, so it is not expected to be registered with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration (DDA). Under Nepal's Drugs Act 2035, drugs must be registered before they are imported or sold.

facts.label: Class
facts.text: An experimental drug that acts on three hormone receptors: GLP-1, GIP and glucagon.

facts.label: Phase 2 result
facts.text: In a 2023 Phase 2 trial, adults with obesity lost up to 24.2% of body weight on average at 48 weeks.

facts.label: Phase 3 status
facts.text: Eli Lilly reported Phase 3 (TRIUMPH) results in 2026 and plans to apply to the FDA in 2027. It is not approved anywhere yet.

facts.label: The glucagon part
facts.text: In animals, glucagon action raised energy use. In people, studies show large drops in liver fat, but whether energy use rises in humans is still being studied.

sources.title: Jastreboff et al., Triple-Hormone-Receptor Agonist Retatrutide for Obesity: A Phase 2 Trial (NEJM 2023)
Eli Lilly: retatrutide Phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 results (July 2026)
Coskun et al., LY3437943, a novel triple agonist (Cell Metabolism 2022, preclinical)

guides.summary: Retatrutide is an experimental drug that acts on three hormone receptors: GLP-1, GIP and glucagon. In a 2023 Phase 2 trial, people lost up to 24.2% of body weight in 48 weeks. It is still being tested and is not approved anywhere.

sections.heading: What retatrutide is
paragraphs: Retatrutide (research code LY3437943) is a single peptide molecule made by Eli Lilly. It is often called a "triple G" agonist because it switches on three receptors.
It is an investigational drug. It is being tested in clinical trials and has not been approved by any regulator.

sections.heading: How it works in the body
paragraphs: GLP-1 receptor: helps insulin release when sugar is high, slows the stomach and reduces appetite in the brain.
GIP receptor: adds to the insulin effect, as with tirzepatide.
Glucagon receptor: this is the new part. Glucagon acts mainly on the liver. In animals, switching on this receptor raised energy use and helped burn fat.
In people, studies show large drops in liver fat. Whether energy use rises in humans is still being studied.
The idea is that appetite reduction (GLP-1 and GIP) plus extra fat use in the liver (glucagon) gives more weight loss than one or two receptors alone.

sections.heading: What the research shows
paragraphs: In a 2023 Phase 2 trial in adults with obesity, the highest dose gave 24.2% average weight loss at 48 weeks. The placebo group lost 2.1%.
Eli Lilly reported results from Phase 3 (TRIUMPH) trials in 2026 and plans to apply to the FDA in 2027.
Until a regulator reviews the full data and approves it, retatrutide remains an experimental medicine.

faq.a: No. It is still in clinical trials and is not approved anywhere. Eli Lilly plans to apply to the FDA in 2027.

faq.q: What makes retatrutide different from tirzepatide?
faq.a: Tirzepatide acts on two receptors (GLP-1 and GIP). Retatrutide adds a third, the glucagon receptor, which acts mainly on the liver.
Yes. Unapproved drugs fall under WADA's S0 non-approved substances rule and are prohibited at all times.

guides.name: GHK-Cu
guides.aka: Copper peptide, copper tripeptide-1, prezatide copper
guides.dopingStatus: Not named on the WADA list, and USADA lists GHK in cosmetics as not prohibited. Injected GHK-Cu is not approved anywhere, so it may fall under WADA's S0 rule. Athletes should check with their anti-doping agency.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Used as a cosmetic ingredient. Not approved as a medicine anywhere, so injectable forms are not expected to be registered with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration.

facts.label: What it is
facts.text: A tiny peptide of three amino acids bound to copper, found naturally in blood. First described by Dr Loren Pickart in 1973.

facts.label: Levels with age
facts.text: Pickart's work reports that blood levels fall with age, from about 200 ng/mL at age 20 to about 80 ng/mL at 60.

facts.label: Gene claims
facts.text: In lab data on human cancer cells, GHK changed the activity of many genes. This was a computer reanalysis by its discoverer, whose company sells GHK products. It does not show the same effects in people.

facts.label: Human evidence
facts.text: Mainly lab and animal studies, plus a few small 12-week skin-cream studies in women. Evidence for hair growth in people is weak. FDA notes limited human data for injectable GHK-Cu.

sources.title: Pickart & Margolina, Regenerative and Protective Actions of the GHK-Cu Peptide in the Light of the New Gene Data (Int J Mol Sci 2018, PubMed 29986520)
Pickart et al., GHK and DNA: resetting the human genome to health (BioMed Res Int 2014, PubMed 25302294; authors affiliated with Skin Biology)
FDA: Certain bulk drug substances for use in compounding that may present significant safety risks (GHK-Cu, injectable)
USADA: Peptides and growth hormones in cosmetics

guides.summary: GHK-Cu is a tiny three-amino-acid peptide bound to copper that is found naturally in blood. Lab and animal studies link it to collagen production and wound healing. Human evidence is mostly small skin-cream studies, and injectable forms are not approved.

sections.heading: What GHK-Cu is
paragraphs: GHK is three amino acids: glycine, histidine and lysine. It holds tightly onto a copper ion, which gives GHK-Cu.
It is found naturally in human blood, saliva and urine. Dr Loren Pickart first described it in 1973.
Pickart's work reports that blood levels fall with age, from about 200 ng/mL at age 20 to about 80 ng/mL at 60.
It is widely used in skin creams, where it may be listed as copper tripeptide-1.

sections.heading: How it is thought to work in the body
paragraphs: Copper carrier: GHK grabs copper and can deliver it to cells. Several repair enzymes need copper to work, including one that links collagen fibers together.
Collagen and skin: in lab studies on skin cells, GHK-Cu increased the production of collagen and other parts of the skin's support structure.
Wound healing: in animal studies, it helped wounds close and attracted repair cells to the area.

Gene activity: a computer reanalysis of lab data found GHK changed the activity of many genes in human cancer cells. This was done by its discoverer, whose company sells GHK products, and it does not show the same effects in people.

sections.heading: What the research actually shows
paragraphs: Most evidence comes from lab and animal studies.
In people, there are a few small 12-week skin-cream studies in women. Evidence for hair growth in people is weak.
The FDA notes limited human data for injectable GHK-Cu and has flagged it as a bulk substance that may present safety risks in compounding.

faq.a: In lab and animal studies, it carried copper to cells, increased collagen production and helped wounds heal. Human evidence is mostly small skin-cream studies.
Yes. GHK is found naturally in human blood. Levels fall with age, from about 200 ng/mL at 20 to about 80 ng/mL at 60, according to its discoverer's research.
It is not named on the WADA list, and USADA lists GHK in cosmetics as not prohibited. Injected GHK-Cu is not approved anywhere, so it may fall under WADA's S0 rule.

quiz.statement: BPC-157 is an FDA-approved medicine for muscle and joint injuries.
quiz.explanation: BPC-157 is not approved by the FDA or any other regulator. Nearly all the evidence comes from rats. A 2026 FDA advisory panel vote about compounding is not an approval, and FDA has not made a final decision.
quiz.reference: FDA, Certain bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks (2026); FDA BPC-157 briefing document (July 2026)

quiz.statement: BPC-157 and TB-500 are banned in all WADA-tested sports.
quiz.explanation: WADA prohibits BPC-157 under S0 (non-approved substances) and TB-500 under S2 (growth factors), both at all times. A first violation for these substances carries a default ban of up to four years.
quiz.reference: WADA 2026 Prohibited List; USADA athlete advisories (2018, 2022)

quiz.statement: Oral BPC-157 has been proven to work in people.
quiz.explanation: Lab tests by BPC-157's developers suggest it survives stomach juice, and it worked by mouth in rats. No human study shows that oral BPC-157 is absorbed or works.
quiz.reference: Sikiric et al., Gut and Liver 2020; FDA BPC-157 briefing document (July 2026)

quiz.statement: Semaglutide and tirzepatide work on exactly the same hormone pathway.
quiz.explanation: Semaglutide acts on the GLP-1 receptor only. Tirzepatide acts on both GLP-1 and GIP receptors. In the SURPASS-2 trial (type 2 diabetes), tirzepatide lowered blood sugar and weight more than semaglutide 1 mg.

quiz.statement: A lab certificate showing high HPLC purity proves a peptide is safe.
quiz.explanation: HPLC and mass spectrometry check purity and identity. They do not show a product is sterile, free of endotoxin, correctly dosed, safe or legal. In a 2024 study, peptides bought online claiming 99% purity failed on several of these.
quiz.reference: Ashraf et al., J Med Internet Res 2024 (doi:10.2196/65440); FDA guidance on synthetic peptide impurities (2021)
